paired_observation.comparison: Aven enters the native overview with two side-by-side windows and reverses to Dolphin. Sampled entry/exit states are restrained. Stock has three windows arranged across two rows, so Aven simplicity cannot be credited as a layout or motion improvement.
paired_observation.limits: Different numbers of applications and window contents; not a matched layout comparison. There is only one sampled intermediate entry state.
paired_observation.aven_detail: Frames 0010–0011 show two window cards settling; frame 0030 shows exit enlargement and overlap; 0031 approaches original geometry; frame 0032 exactly restores initial pixels.

summary: No blocking transition defect appears in these sampled states. Aven fixed-size window fades and the focused preview support the intended calm interaction. Menus, photo crossfades and quick switching largely retain good native behavior.
limitations: Ordered native-frame inspection is not continuous real-time playback.
Requested 10 fps sampling achieved 6.98–8.22 fps stock and 8.44–9.75 fps Aven. Maximum sample gaps are approximately 141–161 ms stock and 128–134 ms Aven.
RFB readback and PNG encoding can omit compositor frames. Host capture-completion times are not physical display-presentation or input-delivery times.
Physical frame pacing, 60 Hz smoothness, exact animation duration and precise input latency remain unverified and unscored.
Window content, geometry and overview window count are not fully matched; visual character can be compared, speed and layout complexity cannot.
Native operation input and pass outcomes are attributed to the verification agent report; critic independently inspected the motion pixels, not all operation stills.
